events.title: First ARPANET host-to-host message
events.summary: On October 29, 1969, UCLA and SRI completed the first ARPANET host-to-host connection — Charley Kline typed "login" and the first two characters "lo" were received before the remote host crashed.
events.about: The link between UCLA's Sigma 7 and SRI's SDS 940 over BBN Interface Message Processors proved packet-switched networking between computers. ARPANET grew to four nodes by December 1969 and became the research network that evolved into the modern internet.

narrative.whyChosen: The first ARPANET login was the proof that computers could talk across a packet network.
narrative.whyImportant: It launched the networking research program that became the global internet.
narrative.problemSolved: Universities and labs needed to share computing resources without dedicated phone lines to every machine.
